findings.text: follow-on: the record lands in the shared crew_home()/watch/senders.jsonl because path.parent is the watch directory common to every project, and the record carries no project, so a watcher stop on a host with several registered projects cannot be attributed to the project whose registration names the signalled pid.

follow-on: the arm logs open with "rev <sha>", where review.recorded_log_revision looks for "revision", so review.annotate_review_of_run records base_log_revision and head_log_revision as None and the added-failure count it derives (0, correctly) cannot be tied to a commit from either log, unlike the sibling node's "revision <sha>" headers.

item_verdicts.diff: read c1e0d6a0 against base f91fa54e; reckon/crew/recovery.py +7 adds one _write_sender_record call before the signal, tests/test_unwatch_leaves_a_sender_record.py +166, the evidence fragment +26; no other file changes.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when names tests/test_unwatch_leaves_a_sender_record.py; the manifest records 2 passed EXIT=0 (head-unwatch.log) and I reproduced 2 passed EXIT=0 here, and the test reads the record at the instant of signalling, asserting it exists, names the live producer pid and reason="unwatch", and that the producer was still alive at the signal.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is that crew unwatch writes a sender record beside the watcher registration before it signals the producer; reckon/crew/recovery.py:7389 calls routing._write_sender_record(path.parent, target_pid=pid, reason="unwatch") immediately before _signal_process_group in unwatch, and path.parent is the directory holding the watch registration, so the goal is met.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, naming the write, its site, the gate, the negative control and the base/head arms with their machine-readable baseline_suite and after_suite JSON; both arm logs open with the token "rev", which review.recorded_log_revision does not match, so their recorded revision reads as None.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the declared paths are reckon/crew/recovery.py, tests/test_unwatch_leaves_a_sender_record.py and the evidence fragment; git show --stat c1e0d6a0 touches exactly those three files and nothing else.

justifications.durability: the declared negative control removes the write and test_unwatch_writes_a_sender_record_before_it_signals reddens on "no sender record on disk when unwatch signalled the producer" (negative-control-unwatch.log, 1 failed 1 passed, EXIT=1), so the guard is verified by reinstating the regression and the record assertion does not move with the value under test.
justifications.evidence: the gate tests/test_unwatch_leaves_a_sender_record.py asserts the done_when measure and its result is recorded in head-unwatch.log and reproduced here (2 passed EXIT=0), but base-arms.log and head-arms.log open with "rev", which review.recorded_log_revision does not recognise, so the added-failure count cannot be tied to a commit from the logs.
justifications.fit: recovery.py:7389 mirrors the existing pre-signal _write_sender_record calls at recovery.py:862 and recovery.py:3040, routing.SENDER_RECORD_NAME holds the filename, and no added name carries a plan, sprint or ticket identifier.
justifications.goal_fidelity: recovery.py:7389 writes the record through routing._write_sender_record into the watch registration's directory before unwatch signals, doing exactly what the goal states; the record carries no project field, so attributing a watcher stop to a project on a multi-project host rests on the pid alone.
justifications.scope_discipline: git show --stat c1e0d6a0 lists exactly the three declared paths and the recovery.py change is a single pre-signal call, carrying nothing the goal does not imply.
